title: metadata: measure the 18.3.0 environment rows that carry the host's stamp in their stored body, and decide whether a stamp-removal migration is owed (follow-up of #32791)
body:
domain:server#7 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgVSjQBHNkZd6Eqx2XX

Follow-up of #32791 (and #32812). Source: #32812's step-0 design and the epic seat's ruling on it. Queued, not dispatched (dispatch is p0/p1 only, ruling 6837849715 on #31527).

## What happens

On 18.3.0 the boot priming pass of a host that declares its package wrote the host's stamp back into the stored body of package-less environment rows. On `main`, `bindReadRowPackage` (ruling 6809488921) binds such a row's package column to the host on first read. So those existing rows count as the host's items under every design #32812 considered (A, B, `main`); #32812 changes only rows the pass reads from now on.

## Owed

1. Measure: on an install that ran 18.3.0 with a host declaring its package and a `DatabaseLoader`, how many environment rows carry the host's stamp, per type, and what each read, write, publish and removal door answers for them after `bindReadRowPackage` binds them.
2. Decide whether a stamp-removal migration is owed. A migration changes who owns existing data in live installs, so after measuring, file a `needs_decision` for the maintainer; do not migrate on this card's own call.
